description:
When Sales By Customer or Sales By Representative is downloaded as a spreadsheet, the numbers arrive dressed up as text. Money comes out as $1,979.40 with a dollar sign and a comma, percentages as 100.0% with a percent sign, and dates as Jul 31 2026.

Because those cells hold text and not numbers, somebody opening the file in Excel cannot add them up, sort them or build a pivot table without cleaning every column first.
steps: Open Reports, then Sales By Customer.
Set the date range to Last Month — 1 to 31 July 2026 — and select the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
Open the three-dot download menu and choose the summary spreadsheet download.
Open the downloaded file in a text editor or Excel and look at the money, percentage and date cells.

Repeat on Reports, then Sales By Representative. This was seen with customer Beman Systems, invoice S-15826 and sales representative Parth Fadadu; both the summary and the expanded downloads behave the same way on both reports.
current:
Sales By Customer, summary download — one row, read straight from the file:

"Beman Systems",0.0,"$1,979.40","$1,979.40","$2,459.48","$2,459.48",$207.84,"$4,438.88",95.5%,"$4,646.72"

The expanded download carries the date the same way: ,,P-126,"Jul 31 2026",0.0,$0.00,…

It is not the date range — the same formatting appears at Last Month, Last Quarter and Last Year. It is not one report or one download: both reports and both downloads do it. On screen the money is correctly shown with dollar signs, which is what the screen is meant to do; the problem is only in the downloaded file.
expected: In the spreadsheets, money is a plain number with no dollar sign and no thousands separators, a percentage is a plain number with no percent sign, and a date is written mm-dd-yyyy.
source: Currency values export as plain numbers with no dollar sign and no thousands separators.
The Margin % cell is a plain number to one decimal with no percent sign (for example, 64.7); it is empty when the row's Subtotal is zero or below.
Dates export as mm-dd-yyyy — for example, 05-14-2026 — matching the ShopView-wide CSV date format.

CSV cell formatting (both CSVs): numeric columns are emitted as plain numbers for re-pivoting — no currency symbol, thousands separators, or parentheses; a negative value uses a leading minus (-1234.56).
